title: Go: Middleware Pipeline
description: Build a composable middleware pipeline in Go inspired by the http.Handler pattern with context propagation and async execution.

steps.title: Middleware type and Handler
steps.description: Define a `Handler` function type that takes and returns a `string` request. Define a `Middleware` type as a function that takes and returns a `Handler`. Implement an `Identity` middleware that passes through unchanged. Test by chaining: `Identity(Identity(upper))` and print the result.
hints: Use `type Handler func(string) string` and `type Middleware func(Handler) Handler`
Identity middleware: `func(h Handler) Handler { return func(s string) string { return h(s) } }`
This is the decorator pattern — each middleware wraps the previous handler

verification.successMessage: Middleware type and identity pass-through work correctly!
verification.failureMessage: Print the result of applying middleware to a handler that uppercases input.

steps.title: Chain execution with context
steps.description: Implement a `Chain` function that composes multiple middlewares into a single handler. Write a `Logger` middleware that prints "[LOG] request" before calling the next handler, and a `Timer` middleware that prints the duration using `time.Since`. Print the final result of the chained execution.
hints: Chain reduces middlewares: `Chain(h, m1, m2, m3)` applies m1(m2(m3(h)))
Logger middleware prints before and after calling the wrapped handler
Timer middleware uses `defer` to measure and print execution duration

verification.successMessage: Middleware chain correctly composes Logger and Timer middlewares!
verification.failureMessage: Print '[LOG] request' and the duration from the Timer middleware.

steps.title: Async middleware with goroutines
steps.description: Create an `Async` middleware that launches the handler in a goroutine and uses a `sync.WaitGroup` to track completion. Implement a `FanOut` middleware that runs the handler multiple times concurrently. Print "Async done" for each completion and collect all results.
hints: Async middleware: `go func() { h(req) }()` with a WaitGroup to signal completion
FanOut takes a count parameter and spawns that many goroutines
Use a `[]string` with a mutex to collect results from multiple goroutines

verification.successMessage: Async middleware correctly executes handlers concurrently in goroutines!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'Async done' each time a goroutine completes.

steps.title: Error recovery middleware
steps.description: Implement a `Recovery` middleware that catches panics from downstream handlers using `defer` and `recover()`. The middleware should print "Panic recovered: <error>" and return a default response instead of crashing. Test by including a handler that panics.
hints: Use `defer func() { if r := recover(); r != nil { ... } }()` at the start of the middleware
On panic, print the recovered error and return a fallback string like "Internal Error"
This pattern is identical to Go HTTP middleware panic recovery

verification.successMessage: Recovery middleware catches panics and returns a graceful fallback response!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'Panic recovered: <error>' and return a fallback response string.

steps.title: Composable router with middleware
steps.description: Build a `Router` struct with method-based routing (GET, POST) and per-route middleware. Support global middleware applied to all routes and route-specific middleware. Register a few routes with different middleware stacks, execute them, and print each handler's response. Use `map[string]http.Handler` internally.
hints: Router holds `routes map[string]Handler` keyed by "METHOD:path" and `global []Middleware`
`Handle(method, path, handler, middlewares...)` stores the composed handler
`Serve(method, path, request)` executes the matching handler and prints the response

verification.successMessage: Composable router correctly applies global and per-route middleware!
verification.failureMessage: Print the handler responses for both GET and POST routes.
